The supported subset comprises eight Ø 2,5 M3 - 6H through holes, two Ø 4,2 M5 - 6H through holes and four vertical 5,5 X 10,0 through slots. Mirrored placements use the printed counts, offsets and pitches. Slot centers derive from the dimensioned lower end-arc center. The original main face-on view establishes that every slot's long axis follows Y, represented explicitly by direction='y'. These are drawing-layout interpretations, not human approvals. Verification: I checked this against the main face-on view of D-013. The plate is 270,0 x 25,0, and its vertical and horizontal dash-dot centerlines set X=0 and Y=0.

M3 holes: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-2 calls for 8 x Ø2,5 THRU ALL, M3 - 6H THRU ALL. All eight sit in one row below the horizontal centerline, at 7,5 (n/7.5@1-1). Dimension 17,9 (n/17.9@1-1) runs from the vertical centerline to the first hole on the right, and 35,7 (n/35.7@1-1) is the pitch. The view shows 4 holes on each side, mirrored about X=0. That gives X = ±17,9, ±53,6, ±89,3 and ±125,0. Each cited expression gives the right value, for example 17,9+3*35,7=125,0.

M5 holes: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-1 calls for 2 x Ø4,2 THRU ALL, M5 - 6H. Dimension 82,0 (n/82.0@1-1) runs from the left hole to the vertical centerline, and the right hole is drawn as its mirror. Both holes sit 4,5 above the centerline (n/4.5@1-1), so Y=+4,5.

Slots: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-3 calls for 4 x 5,5 X 10,0 THRU ALL, and all four are drawn with their long axis vertical, so direction='y' is correct. Dimension 41,0 (n/41.0@1-1) runs from the centerline to the inner right slot, and 82,0 (n/82.0@1-2) is the slot-to-slot pitch. The left slots mirror the right ones, giving X = ±41 and ±123. Dimension 2,3 (n/2.3@1-1) runs from the centerline to the centre of the slot's lower end arc, so the slot centre is at 2,3+(10,0-5,5)/2=4,55. The view supports this: the slot centres line up with the M5 row, which would not happen if 2,3 measured to the slot centre.

All the cuts are through cuts, so assigning them to the top face is valid. The Ø2,5 and Ø4,2 drill sizes are printed on the drawing, not inferred from the thread sizes. The supported subset comprises eight Ø 2,5 M3 - 6H through holes, two Ø 4,2 M5 - 6H through holes and four vertical 5,5 X 10,0 through slots. Mirrored placements use the printed counts, offsets and pitches. Slot centers derive from the dimensioned lower end-arc center. The original main face-on view establishes that every slot's long axis follows Y, represented explicitly by direction='y'. These are drawing-layout interpretations, not human approvals. Verification: I checked this against the main face-on view of D-013. The plate is 270,0 x 25,0, and its vertical and horizontal dash-dot centerlines set X=0 and Y=0.

M3 holes: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-2 calls for 8 x Ø2,5 THRU ALL, M3 - 6H THRU ALL. All eight sit in one row below the horizontal centerline, at 7,5 (n/7.5@1-1). Dimension 17,9 (n/17.9@1-1) runs from the vertical centerline to the first hole on the right, and 35,7 (n/35.7@1-1) is the pitch. The view shows 4 holes on each side, mirrored about X=0. That gives X = ±17,9, ±53,6, ±89,3 and ±125,0. Each cited expression gives the right value, for example 17,9+3*35,7=125,0.

M5 holes: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-1 calls for 2 x Ø4,2 THRU ALL, M5 - 6H. Dimension 82,0 (n/82.0@1-1) runs from the left hole to the vertical centerline, and the right hole is drawn as its mirror. Both holes sit 4,5 above the centerline (n/4.5@1-1), so Y=+4,5.

Slots: Callout D-013/drawing/callout/p1-3 calls for 4 x 5,5 X 10,0 THRU ALL, and all four are drawn with their long axis vertical, so direction='y' is correct. Dimension 41,0 (n/41.0@1-1) runs from the centerline to the inner right slot, and 82,0 (n/82.0@1-2) is the slot-to-slot pitch. The left slots mirror the right ones, giving X = ±41 and ±123. Dimension 2,3 (n/2.3@1-1) runs from the centerline to the centre of the slot's lower end arc, so the slot centre is at 2,3+(10,0-5,5)/2=4,55. The view supports this: the slot centres line up with the M5 row, which would not happen if 2,3 measured to the slot centre.

All the cuts are through cuts, so assigning them to the top face is valid. The Ø2,5 and Ø4,2 drill sizes are printed on the drawing, not inferred from the thread sizes.
